The final wheat output will depend significantly on weather patterns influenced by El Nino in April and May. El Nino typically brings above-average rainfall to key wheat-growing areas but may also increase flooding risks. Adequate snow cover from expected precipitation could benefit both overwintering crops and reservoir replenishment.

items.title: Keralam testing random fuel samples for ethanol density: State Minister Anoop Jacob says 'major concern' raised in Karnataka
items.summary: Keralam's Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob recently declared a program to collect petrol samples for ethanol testing, aiming to address concerns voiced by Karnataka officials regarding excessive ethanol blending. Jacob underscored the necessity of consumer transparency regarding fuel components, noting that inspections in Kochi have uncovered samples currently being tested, thus igniting pivotal discussions about fuel quality across Indian states.

items.title: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod to float IPO
items.summary: MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary, MMT India, has received approval from Sebi for an initial public offering. This approval follows a confidential filing of draft papers made in July. The IPO will involve the sale of equity shares by MakeMyTrip and its subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings. Proceeds from the sale are expected to enhance the cash position of the parent company.

items.title: Bengaluru-Mangaluru Vande Bharat would take just 7 hours to travel between the two cities, saving up to 9 hours compared with other express trains; check launch date and stops
items.summary: Bengaluru-Mangaluru Vande Bharat will start within weeks, said Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. In trials, it took about 7 hours, saving 2 to 9 hours over existing trains. A flight takes about an hour but costs Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,700. The fare and final timetable are awaited.

items.title: Indian bonds drift with oil; inflation data in focus
items.summary: Indian government bonds exhibited limited movement today as oil prices showed signs of stabilization. Investors are remaining cautious, especially with inflation data from both the United States and India on the horizon. Scheduled for later today is a bond auction totaling 290.5 billion rupees. Analysts predict yields on the 10-year bond could oscillate between 7.30% and 7.10%, with particular attention on India's October inflation report due for release this Thursday.

items.title: Explained: Why Nvidia shares dropped 4% in overnight trade and what analysts warn can trigger a bloodbath?
items.summary: Nvidia shares dropped over 4% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice, a Chinese national, raised security concerns following intelligence reports. Nvidia has initiated an investigation into these allegations, although the board believes no secrets were compromised. Analysts suggest the company's upcoming earnings report will be crucial for market sentiment. Concerns linger over Huang's position if further evidence of wrongdoing emerges.

items.summary: Adoration for the US tech giant’s CEO Jensen Huang has been labelled “Jensanity”, but can his reputation survive the news of his affair?

items.title: Vande Bharat Sleeper is not offering some features passengers are used to on regular trains: No Tatkal, no RAC, no waiting list and fixed fares; check all the rules before booking
items.summary: The newly introduced Vande Bharat Sleeper trains are expected to make long-distance overnight journeys more comfortable, but passengers should be aware of a few important booking rules before planning their trips. Indian Railways has kept some features of the regular reservation system out of these premium services. Tatkal bookings will not be permitted, ticket prices will not follow a dynamic fare system, and passengers will be able to book only confirmed berths. Here is a look at the reservation rules, coach configuration and berth availability on Vande Bharat Sleeper trains.

items.title: Nvidia stock in focus: 3 key risks after Jensen Huang probe
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces scrutiny after the company launched an independent probe into allegations that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The controversy has raised concerns over leadership, corporate governance, China-related business and investor confidence.

items.title: Nuvama Wealth Management Q2 Results: Profit rises 19% YoY to Rs 304 crore
items.summary: Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd achieved a consolidated net profit of Rs 303.5 crore for Q2 FY27. The company saw a revenue increase of 20.35% to Rs 1,366 crore for the same quarter. Client assets reached Rs 5.5 lakh crore, reflecting a 25% year-on-year growth. Wealth management, asset services, and capital markets drove this substantial growth. The company demonstrated strong operating profits with a return on equity remaining robust at 29%.

items.title: Nvidia falls about 3% in after-hours and perpetual futures trade
items.summary: Nvidia's shares saw a decline in after-hours trading following an announcement regarding CEO Jensen Huang. The company indicated that it is investigating potential foreign intelligence efforts aimed at Huang. Perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange and shares trading on the Blue Ocean system reflected this drop in value. The share price fell approximately 3.4% compared to Friday's Nasdaq closing price.

items.title: Gold's short-term volatility contrasts with long-term bullishness
items.summary: Recently, gold prices have leveled out at approximately $4,000 an ounce after experiencing notable volatility throughout the year. This stabilization has attracted increased investor interest, spurred by central bank acquisitions amid economic unpredictability. Moreover, demand for gold jewelry has seen a significant uptick in regions like India and China, thanks to decreased prices.

items.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen safely evacuated, Embassy says
items.summary: The Embassy of India to Yemen has evacuated 19 Indian seafarers who were stranded in Hodeidah and Sana'a. All seafarers are reported to be safe and in good health while returning to India. India has lost a total of 23 nationals amid ongoing conflicts in West Asia, including Indian seafarers and others in shipping attacks.

items.title: 'Global insurance cover may help rise medical tourism': Apollo Hospitals' Sangita Reddy
items.summary: Apollo Hospitals envisions that broadening insurance access for international patients will catalyze the growth of medical tourism in India. The medical travel industry is predicted to swell to about $286.1 billion by 2030, with India's share expected to be around $16.2 billion. The focus on preventive health check-ups is essential for timely detection and holistic wellness. Additionally, artificial intelligence is poised to significantly transform healthcare service delivery and patient interaction.

items.title: Gold, silver prices may sway with US-Iran tensions
items.summary: As the US-Iran conflict and crude oil pricing remain in focus, bullion prices are set to encounter downward pressure. Key economic data releases from China, the US, Germany, Japan, and India will significantly impact inflation and interest rate expectations. Market watchers will be attentive to Federal Reserve remarks and US job market indicators for cues on trends.

items.title: Oil falls on open as Trump says fresh Iran attacks 'unlikely'
items.summary: Oil prices fell at the start of the week as uncertainties regarding military actions persist. US President Donald Trump suggested that further attacks on Iran are unlikely while diplomatic talks are ongoing. The tensions surround recent incidents affecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil passage. Brent crude oil prices declined by 64 cents, while West Texas Intermediate prices also saw a reduction.

items.title: Iraq reaches US understanding to resume oil exports through Strait of Hormuz, says foreign minister
items.summary: Iraq has reached an understanding with the US to allow its oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz using a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said. Iraq's losses from the Iran war and disruptions to oil shipments have reached $60 billion. Exports recovered to 3.5 million bpd in October.
